people.name: Olivia O'Brien
people.description: American singer, songwriter, and actress Olivia O'Brien achieved fame in 2016 through her collaboration with Gnash on the single 'I Hate U, I Love U'. The track reached No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in the United States and claimed the No. 1 spot in Australia.

people.name: Rita Ora
people.description: Rita Ora is a British singer-songwriter and actress. Her debut studio album, Ora (2012), entered the UK charts at No. 1 and included the No. 1 hit singles 'R.I.P.' and 'How We Do (Party)'.

people.name: Benjamin Wysocki
people.description: Benjamin Wysocki is the drummer for the American rock band The Fray. The group achieved a 2005 US Top 3 single with 'How to Save a Life'. In 2009, their second, self-titled album was released and debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard charts.

people.name: Natasha Bedingfield
people.description: British singer and songwriter Natasha Bedingfield achieved a UK No.1 single in 2004 with 'These Words'. She earned a Grammy Award nomination for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance for 'Unwritten', alongside nominations for Best British Female Artist at the 2005 and 2006 Brit Awards.

people.name: Beau  Dozier
people.description: American songwriter and record producer Beau Dozier collaborated with chart-topping artists across various genres, such as Tupac Shakur, Snoop Dogg, Priscilla Ahn, Boyz II Men, The Backstreet Boys, and Jennifer Lopez. His father, Lamont Dozier (1941 – 2022), gained recognition primarily as part of the Motown songwriting and production team Holland–Dozier–Holland. Beau Dozier passed away on 8 March 2025 at the age of 45.

people.name: Ron Jones
people.description: Ron Jones, guitar, The Flaming Lips. Their 1999 release The Soft Bulletin was NME magazine's Album of the Year and the group has won three Grammy Awards.

people.name: John Stirratt
people.description: John Stirratt serves as the bassist for the American alternative rock band Wilco, which released the albums Yankee Hotel Foxtrot, A Ghost Is Born, Sky Blue Sky, and Wilco (The Album).

people.name: Mark Gillespie
people.description: Mark Gillespie was a member of the British boy band Big Fun. The group achieved a No.4 single on the UK chart in 1989 with 'Blame It On The Boogie', which was a cover version of a 1978 hit by The Jacksons. Their sole album, A Pocketful of Dreams, came out in 1990 and entered the top 10 of the UK Albums Chart.

people.name: Adam Gaynor
people.description: Adam Gaynor played guitar for Matchbox Twenty, a band that achieved global recognition through their debut album, Yourself or Someone Like You (1996). The album earned a 12x Platinum certification in the United States, alongside multi-platinum certifications in Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

people.name: Martin Lee
people.description: Martin Lee was an English singer and songwriter and a member of the pop group Brotherhood of Man. The group achieved a 1976 hit with 'Save Your Kisses for Me', which served as the United Kingdom's entry in the Eurovision Song Contest 1976. This track became a worldwide success and attained the No. 1 position across numerous nations, such as the UK, where it emerged as the top-selling single of that year. Lee passed away on 29 September 2024 at the age of 77.

people.name: John Rossall
people.description: John Rossall was part of the Glitter Band, an English glam rock group that initially served as Gary Glitter's backing band starting in 1973 before launching their own recording career. As a band, they secured a 1974 UK No.4 single with "Angel Face".

people.name: Raymond Louis Kennedy
people.description: Raymond Louis Kennedy was an American singer, songwriter, musician, and record producer. He co-wrote 'Sail On, Sailor', which was one of The Beach Boys' mid-career hits, along with two hits for The Babys titled 'Everytime I Think of You' and 'Isn't It Time'. Additionally, he collaborated with Jeff Beck, Aerosmith, Willie Nelson, Sly and the Family Stone, and various other acts.

people.name: Burt Reiter
people.description: Burt Reiter played bass for the Dutch rock band Focus. The group achieved a UK No. 4 single in 1973 with 'Sylvia' and a US No. 9 single in 1973 with 'Hocus Pocus'.

people.name: John McVie
people.description: British bass guitarist John McVie played in John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers before joining Fleetwood Mac, which achieved a UK No.1 hit in 1968 with 'Albatross', along with the hits 'Man of the World' and 'Oh Well'. In 1977, the band achieved a US No.1 single with 'Dreams' from their worldwide No.1 album Rumours, which spent 31 weeks on the US chart. McVie married blues pianist and singer Christine Perfect in 1968, and she joined Fleetwood Mac two years later. Although John and Christine McVie divorced in 1976, they maintained their professional collaboration.

people.name: Michael Omartian
people.description: Michael Omartian is an American singer-songwriter, arranger, keyboardist, and music producer who achieved No.1 records across three consecutive decades. He has received 11 Grammy Award nominations and secured three wins, which include honors for Christopher Cross's 'Sailing'. Throughout his career, Omartian has performed on or produced records for Rod Stewart, Steely Dan, Michael Jackson, Whitney Houston, Dolly Parton, Donna Summer, and Billy Joel.

people.name: Alan Henderson
people.description: Alan Henderson served as the bassist for the Northern Irish group Them. Alongside Van Morrison, who provided lead vocals, the band achieved UK chart success in 1965 with the tracks 'Baby, Please Don't Go' and 'Here Comes The Night'. After Morrison departed the group in 1966, he pursued a successful solo career.

people.name: Jean Terrell
people.description: American R&B and jazz vocalist Jean Terrell took over from Diana Ross as the lead singer of the Supremes in 1970. At the start of the new decade, the group achieved further chart success with tracks such as 'Up the Ladder to the Roof', 'Stoned Love', 'River Deep – Mountain High' alongside the Four Tops, 'Nathan Jones', and 'Floy Joy'.

people.name: David White
people.description: David White was an American singer-songwriter who helped create and belonged to the founding lineup of the doo-wop group Danny & the Juniors and the pop trio The Spokesmen. He composed the rock and roll anthem 'Rock and Roll is Here to Stay' and co-wrote several other hits, such as 'At the Hop,' which was performed by Danny & the Juniors. He passed away in Las Vegas on March 16, 2019, at the age of 79.

people.name: Tina Turner
people.description: American singer, songwriter Tina Turner (Annie Mae Bullock) achieved success alongside Ike & Tina Turner with the 1966 UK No.3 single 'River Deep Mountain High', the 1971 US No.4 single 'Proud Mary', and 1973's 'Nutbush City Limits', before scoring solo hits including the 1984 US No.1 single 'What's Love Got To Do With It' and over 25 additional Top 40 singles. Recognized as one of the world's best-selling artists of all time and referred to as The Queen of Rock 'n' Roll, Turner is among the most successful female Rock 'n' Roll artists and received eleven Grammy Awards. Turner passed away on 24 May 2023 following a long illness that included cancer, strokes, and kidney failure.

people.name: Bob Babbitt
people.description: Hungarian-American bassist, Bob Babbitt most famous for his work as a member of Motown Records' studio band, the Funk Brothers, from 1966 to 1972. Babbitt's most notable bass performances include 'Signed, Sealed, Delivered I'm Yours' by Stevie Wonder, 'War' by Edwin Starr, 'The Tears of a Clown' by Smokey Robinson & the Miracles, 'Mercy Mercy Me (The Ecology)' and 'Inner City Blues' by Marvin Gaye, 'Band Of Gold' by Freda Payne, 'Ball of Confusion (That's What the World Is Today)', and 'Just My Imagination (Running Away With Me)' by The Temptations. Bob Babbitt died on July 16, 2012, aged 74, from brain cancer.

people.name: Michael Holliday
people.description: British singer Michael Holliday who had the 1958 UK No.1 'The Story Of My Life'. The song gave the writers Bacharach and David their first UK No.1 hit. According to Elvis Costello, while working as a seaman in the Merchant Navy, Holliday used to smuggle obscure US jazz records into the UK, where Costello's mother, Lilian Ablett, sold them. Holliday died on 29 Oct 1963 age 38.

works.eventDescription: Adele was at No.1 on the UK chart with her fourth studio album 30. Her first studio album in six years following 25 (2015) the album was nominated for six Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year, and won the Brit Award for British Album of the Year at the Brit Awards 2022, making Adele the first solo artist in history to win the award three times, having won previously for 21 and 25. 30 reached No.1 in twenty-five countries.

works.title: Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain
works.eventDescription: While travelling from Los Angeles to Texas, Willie Nelson was arrested when six ounces of marijuana were discovered in his tour bus. Following a $2,500 bail payment, he was released. Due to the small quantity of marijuana, prosecutor Kit Bramblett did not support a jail sentence for Nelson, proposing a $100 fine instead and remarking that he would require Nelson to perform 'Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain' for the court.

works.title: Slow Motion
works.eventDescription: At the age of 25, rapper Soulja Slim was shot and killed outside his residence in New Orleans. He appeared on the 2004 US No. 1 single 'Slow Motion' by Juvenile.

works.title: Beatles 1
works.eventDescription: The Beatles topped the US album chart with 'Beatles 1.' The release contains practically every number-one single put out between 1962 and 1970. Coming out on the 30th anniversary of the band's break-up, it marked their first compilation offered on a single CD. As the global best-selling album of the 21st century, 1 has surpassed 31 million copies sold.

works.title: I'll Make Love to You
works.eventDescription: 'I'll Make Love To You' by Boyz II Men marked the group's 14th and final week at the top of the US singles chart, equaling the longest chart run in history, which was shared with Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You'.

works.title: I Will Always Love You
works.eventDescription: 'I'll Make Love To You' by Boyz II Men marked the group's 14th and final week at the top of the US singles chart, equaling the longest chart run in history, which was shared with Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You'.

works.title: Hell Freezes Over
works.eventDescription: With the release of 'Hell Freezes Over,' the Eagles began a two-week period at No. 1 on the US album chart. The title of the album derives from a statement made by Don Henley following the group's 1980 split, when he remarked that they would reunite only when hell freezes over.

works.title: Delicate Sound of Thunder
works.eventDescription: Soyuz 7 Russian cosmonauts carried a cassette of the newest Pink Floyd album, Delicate Sound Of Thunder, into space—omitting the plastic case to save weight—and played it in orbit. This achievement made Pink Floyd the initial rock band broadcast in space. Both Nick Mason and David Gilmour were present at the spacecraft's launch.

works.title: Anarchy in the U.K.
works.eventDescription: The Sex Pistols put out the single 'Anarchy In The UK'. Initially packaged in a plain black sleeve, the single served as the sole Sex Pistols recording issued by EMI, climbing to No.38 on the UK Singles Chart prior to EMI dropping the band on 6 January 1977.

works.title: Farewell Concert
works.artist: Allan J R Thomson, Bob Wallace
works.eventDescription: Cream performed their final concert at London's Royal Albert Hall, sharing the bill with Yes and Taste. The performance was captured on film and distributed as Cream's Farewell Concert, a release frequently criticized for subpar audio and visual quality, notably featuring a careless post-editing error during Ginger Baker's drum solo that makes him appear to change clothes instantly.

works.title: Hello Goodbye
works.eventDescription: The Beatles broadcast a promotional clip for their song 'Hello, Goodbye' on the television program hosted by Ed Sullivan in the United States. At that time, the video did not air in the United Kingdom because of a ban by the musicians' union against miming.

works.title: Please Please Me
works.eventDescription: The Beatles recorded their second single, "Please Please Me," in 18 takes, along with the B-side "Ask Me Why" at EMI studios in London. Upon its United States release on the Vee-Jay label, initial pressings contained a typo that misspelled the group's name as "The Beattles".

works.eventDescription: Johnny Cash entered the US country chart for the first time as 'Cry! Cry! Cry!' reached number 14. Following this, his subsequent seven singles all placed within the country top 10, including 'I Walk the Line' and 'There You Go', both of which secured the number 1 position.

works.title: Signed sealed delivered I'm yours
works.eventDescription: Hungarian-American bassist, Bob Babbitt most famous for his work as a member of Motown Records' studio band, the Funk Brothers, from 1966 to 1972. Babbitt's most notable bass performances include 'Signed, Sealed, Delivered I'm Yours' by Stevie Wonder, 'War' by Edwin Starr, 'The Tears of a Clown' by Smokey Robinson & the Miracles, 'Mercy Mercy Me (The Ecology)' and 'Inner City Blues' by Marvin Gaye, 'Band Of Gold' by Freda Payne, 'Ball of Confusion (That's What the World Is Today)', and 'Just My Imagination (Running Away With Me)' by The Temptations. Bob Babbitt died on July 16, 2012, aged 74, from brain cancer.

works.title: The Story of My Life
works.eventDescription: British singer Michael Holliday who had the 1958 UK No.1 'The Story Of My Life'. The song gave the writers Bacharach and David their first UK No.1 hit. According to Elvis Costello, while working as a seaman in the Merchant Navy, Holliday used to smuggle obscure US jazz records into the UK, where Costello's mother, Lilian Ablett, sold them. Holliday died on 29 Oct 1963 age 38.
